handoff.summary: Four current-account/price definitions: GNP residence adjustment, net domestic product, signed personal saving, and implicit deflator. b01/b02 IDs preserved. Accounts use current-price flows; implicit deflator alone pairs matching nominal and chained values. All numerical oracles are explicitly synthetic independent ledger/limiting checks rather than claimed published national statistics.
gaps: All four require economics quantities/context and reference-year currency conventions beyond runtime snapshot.
BEA citing policies inspected; full redistribution terms not established, with no agency endorsement or universal clearance inferred.
A scalar numeric guard cannot check residency, current-account classification, reference year or vintage consistency.
handoff.review_notes: Inspected direct BEA glossary/FAQ definitions and precise handbook passages on 2026-11-01. Reviewed residency rather than citizenship, CFC current-cost/economic-life basis, ordinary versus disaster loss, complete personal outlays, signed saving, and price-index levels versus growth. Arithmetic, domains and inverse singularities reviewed. Actual toolkit JSON/ZIP validation logs accompany the return. Duplicate search includes all prior own batches and supplied 37-record inventory/runtime snapshot only; scientific review remains pending. Toolkit JSON validation passed: four models, 11 arithmetic and six rejection checks, all requires-extension. Final prose edit revalidated before packing.

models.title: Current-price GNP from GDP and cross-border income
models.summary: Accounting change from domestic production to production attributable to resident labor and property. Residence-based scope is distinct from citizenship, location of sales or ownership of all output from a foreign plant.

relationship.original_equation: GNP = GDP + income receipts from the rest of the world - income payments to the rest of the world.
relationship.locator: Chapter 2, Geographic coverage, printed p.2-6 (PDF p.6); GNP definition on 2-13 (PDF p.13)
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced R and P label the source's gross directional income receipts/payments; GDP and GNP retained. Currency+currency-currency=currency. Components are current interval flows on matching price/vintage bases. No gross plant output abroad is added: only the income attributable to resident labor/property is included. Do not substitute export/import values, capital transfers or a person's full foreign remittance. No statistical discrepancy correction is silently applied; the handbook distinguishes GNI as a separately estimated income measure.

Resident-attributable total is 800+150=950, while domestic output is 1000. No other flows. Cross-checks production location against residence attribution rather than rearranging the same three supplied terms.

models.inverse_notes: Given GNP,R,P, GDP=GNP-R+P; given GNP,GDP,P, R=GNP-GDP+P; given GNP,GDP,R, P=GDP+R-GNP. Each additive inverse is unique with all other amounts known, no denominator restrictions. Ledger check GNP=950,GDP=1000,R=150 yields P=200 and forward GNP=950. If GDP=GNP and R is zero, recovered P=0; no singularity. If only GDP and GNP are known, R and P remain underdetermined even if both are zero in one possible case. Inverses do not infer causal effects or residency classifications.

gaps: New GNP and cross-border-income meanings; reuse b01 current-price GDP only at matched NIPA context. No monetary unit extension alone can establish the resident attribution.

models.title: Current-price net domestic product
models.summary: Domestic gross production net of the fixed capital consumed in producing it. A net flow of production, retaining the distinction from capital stocks, capital gains and catastrophic asset losses.

relationship.locator: BEA NDP Glossary definition; NIPA Chapter 2 printed p.2-13 (PDF p.13)
relationship.translation_notes: Source symbols retained. Dimensions currency-currency=currency; GDP and CFC are flows over the same interval, not a current-dollar output minus the opening asset stock. NIPA CFC is current-cost economic depreciation rather than a tax/book depreciation schedule. Keep signed net output: the definition does not impose CFC<=GDP or clip a negative result. Nominal scope selected to avoid subtracting incompatible separately chained real measures.

variables.definition: Current-price gross domestic production during the accounting interval.
variables.context: Same domestic economy and current-production accounting interval, current-price USD, source vintage and seasonal/annual-rate basis. CFC must have NIPA current replacement-cost valuation/economic service lives for domestic fixed assets; ordinary depreciation and catastrophic losses are distinguished.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative in this positive gross-production profile.

variables.definition: Current-cost charge for domestic private/government fixed capital used up through normal wear, aging, obsolescence and ordinary accidental damage during the interval.
variables.context: Same domestic economy and current-production accounting interval, current-price USD, source vintage and seasonal/annual-rate basis. CFC must have NIPA current replacement-cost valuation/economic service lives for domestic fixed assets; ordinary depreciation and catastrophic losses are distinguished.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative flow; excludes catastrophic loss and pure holding gains/losses; not historical-cost tax depreciation.

variables.definition: Current-price domestic production after replacing the fixed capital consumed in producing it.
variables.context: Same domestic economy and current-production accounting interval, current-price USD, source vintage and seasonal/annual-rate basis. variables.domain: Finite signed net production; no universal nonnegative net-product condition imposed.

assumptions: Source definition: deduct consumption of fixed capital from gross domestic production.
Source convention: NIPA CFC uses current-cost valuation/economic lives and excludes catastrophic asset loss.
Application profile: nonnegative gross production and CFC; identical interval, price basis and vintage.
limitations: Does not estimate CFC, use a depreciation rate, or update a capital stock.
No welfare/sustainability prediction; subtraction alone does not establish feasible future consumption. Independently chained real series require separate aggregation review.

references.method: Independent capital-use ledger: all 50 current output units replace part of 80 capital units consumed at one dollar each; 30 units of existing capital are not replaced. Net available product is a 30-dollar shortfall. This illustrates signed net arithmetic, not a disaster charge.

models.inverse_notes: GDP=NDP+CFC given NDP,CFC, retaining GDP>=0,CFC>=0; CFC=GDP-NDP given GDP,NDP, retaining CFC>=0,GDP>=0. Unique additive solutions with no denominator. Ordinary ledger NDP=920,CFC=80 gives GDP=1000 and forward 920. At CFC=0 recovered GDP=NDP; zero case is nonsingular. A requested inverse with NDP>GDP yields negative CFC and is rejected by original profile; negative NDP itself is allowed. No inference of a capital stock or depreciation schedule.

models.title: Personal saving from income, outlays and current taxes
models.summary: Signed NIPA current saving of persons; consumption, personal interest and current transfers belong in outlays. Includes dissaving and excludes revaluation of existing assets from saving.

relationship.original_equation: Personal saving = personal income - personal outlays - personal current taxes.
relationship.locator: Glossary Personal saving; corroborated Chapter 2 printed 2-7 and Account 3 on 2-30 (PDF pp.7 and 30)
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced PI,O,T,S map precise prose labels; no arbitrary household cash budget is claimed to equal the national aggregate. Dimensions currency-currency-currency=currency. PI includes source-defined current transfers and imputed income, so it is not merely wages or cash income; O is not merely PCE; T is personal current taxes. No nonnegative-saving restriction: signed outlays/income values retain NIPA measurement conventions. Asset-sale proceeds or borrowed principal are funding transactions, not extra PI in this identity. A no-capital-gain synthetic budget is used only for an independent oracle.

models.inverse_notes: PI=S+O+T, O=PI-T-S, T=PI-O-S with all other values known and source accounting conventions retained. All additive directions unique; no zero exclusions or roots. models.title: Implicit price deflator of a corresponding current/chained series
models.summary: Index-level accounting ratio on a reference-year-equals-100 scale. Distinguishes current-dollar activity from its corresponding chained-dollar activity; does not reconstruct the chain index from commodity data.

relationship.locator: BEA Glossary IPD; NIPA Chapter 4 printed p.4-27 (PDF p.27)
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced D=source IPD, N=current-dollar series, R=corresponding chained-dollar series. Both monetary numerics use the same USD scale but different price bases, so ratio yields the price-level index. Dimensions currency/currency=1; literal 100 normalizes index points, not percent inflation. This is the implicit deflator formula, neither Laspeyres nor Paasche nor a newly assumed fixed basket. Basket/coverage is precisely that of the input aggregate's official chain-type quantity series; the reference year is an input context, not fixed to 2017 by this reusable definition. Positive-series profile excludes zero/negative component levels for which a positive price index may be uninterpretable. No pixel-based PDF formula claim needed: direct official glossary prose defines the ratio completely.

variables.definition: Current-price value of the same GDP or eligible aggregate in the current interval.
variables.context: Same strictly positive BEA GDP or eligible series, geography/coverage, current interval and revision vintage; nominal current USD and corresponding chained reference-year USD level share scale and annual-rate/seasonal convention. Reference year and full underlying chain-type basket/weight methodology explicitly accompany real series.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive in this price-index profile; aggregate identity/coverage provided in context.

assumptions: Source definition: numerator is current-dollar value and denominator its corresponding chained-dollar value, multiplied by 100.

references.method: Independent two-good uniform-price construction: reference prices 2 and 5 dollars, reference quantities 100 and 60 (value 500); current quantities 150 and 50 (reference-price value 550). All current prices exactly 1.2 times reference prices, so both Laspeyres and Paasche price relatives, and Fisher, are 1.2 independently of basket substitution. Current prices are 2.4 and 6, giving 360+300=660. A one-link chain anchored to the reference yields real 550 and price level 120. Tolerance floating only.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic uniform-price two-good oracle; not published BEA data. Chain methodology support: chapter 4 and official glossary.

references.method: Limiting reference-year identity: current-dollar and chained reference-year value coincide, so the deflator's normalization is 100, not zero.

Independent homogeneous basket with unchanged quantities and every price falling by one tenth; current spending 450 on base basket value 500 implies price level 90. No inflation-rate input is mistaken for an index level.

Zero nominal series is outside the positive-price-index profile, even though algebra would yield zero.

models.inverse_notes: N=D*R/100 given D>0,R>0; R=100*N/D given N>0,D>0. Unique positive solutions; denominator 100 fixed and nonzero, D must be positive for the latter direction. Synthetic substitution D=120,R=550 gives N=660; forward 120. At D=100, N=R uniquely for known one of them. Zero D and zero N could otherwise leave R arbitrary, but both are outside original positive-series profile. No inverse solves the underlying commodity basket or price vector; no statistical/counterfactual inference.
